title: Understanding Bias and Variance
text: Bias refers to the error introduced by approximating a real-world problem, which may be complex, by a simplified model. Variance refers to how much the model's predictions would change if we used a different training dataset.

title: Effect of More Data on Bias
text: Adding more data points generally helps in reducing the variance of the model but does not necessarily affect the bias. Bias is more related to the model's assumptions.

title: Effect of More Data on Variance
text: Increasing the number of data points typically reduces the variance because the model has more information to learn from, leading to more stable predictions.

title: Evaluating the Statement
